Age.description: Seconds since the cached response was stored (cache hits only).

Link.description: `<url>; rel="help"`: help link an administrator attached to this error (buffered responses only).

RateLimit.description: IETF RateLimit for the tightest quota: `limit=<n>, remaining=<n>, reset=<seconds>` (`reset` omitted for lifetime windows). Present when a quota or budget applies to the request (on success, on later errors and on streams). Values are a snapshot taken before the upstream call: this request's request count is included, its tokens and spend are not.

RateLimit-Policy.description: IETF RateLimit-Policy: one item per enforced quota, `<limit>;w=<window seconds>;qu="<metric>";id="<quota id>"` (`w` omitted for lifetime windows; spend in USD). Present when a quota or budget applies to the request (on success, on later errors and on streams). Values are a snapshot taken before the upstream call: this request's request count is included, its tokens and spend are not.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (quota and limit refusals, no available target, or relayed from the provider).

X-Quilr-Attempts.description: Number of upstream sends made, same-target retries included. Only sent when greater than 1; also on errors.

X-Quilr-Budget-Overflow.description: `true` when a quota admitted this request inside its overflow band (at or over its limit but under the hard stop).

X-Quilr-Cache.description: `HIT` or `MISS` when the app's response cache is on and the request was eligible (non-streaming Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, Embeddings). Absent on bypass. Send `Cache-Control: no-cache` to skip the lookup (the response is still stored) or `no-store` to skip both.

X-Quilr-Error-Code.description: The error code (see `x-quilr-error-codes`). Sent on upstream failures, routing and translation errors, and Bedrock and Google-format errors that carry a gateway code; elsewhere the code is in the body.

X-Quilr-Error-Source.description: `upstream` when the provider failed (status and scrubbed reason relayed), `gateway` for the gateway's own routing refusals.

X-Quilr-Failover.description: Failover tier of the target that served, when it was not the first choice: `route` (another member of the route), `fallback` (an explicit fallback), `same_model` (the same model on another provider) or `app` (another target of the app). Also on errors.

X-Quilr-Quota-Blocked-By.description: Comma-separated ids of every quota that refused the request (429).

X-Quilr-Quota-Id.description: Id of the primary exhausted quota (429 `quota_exceeded`).

X-Quilr-Quota-Remaining.description: Remaining allowance of the tightest quota (USD for spend). Present when a quota or budget applies to the request (on success, on later errors and on streams). Values are a snapshot taken before the upstream call: this request's request count is included, its tokens and spend are not.

X-Quilr-Quota-Reset.description: Reset time of the tightest quota (ISO 8601 UTC); omitted for lifetime windows. Present when a quota or budget applies to the request (on success, on later errors and on streams). Values are a snapshot taken before the upstream call: this request's request count is included, its tokens and spend are not.

X-Quilr-Quota-Scope.description: `node`: quota counters are kept per gateway node; `shared`: counters are shared by every gateway node in the region. Sent whenever any quota header is.

X-Quilr-Quota-Warning.description: `id=<quota id>; pct=<used percent>`: the most-used quota at or past one of its alert thresholds.

X-Quilr-Request-ID.description: Gateway request id (UUID). Quote it to support. Sent on every response of Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, Embeddings and Bedrock Runtime, and on streams the gateway had to commit early; on other APIs only on errors rewritten by an administrator's friendly-error rule.

X-Quilr-Route.description: Opaque, stable id of the routing rule that chose the upstream: `r_` plus 16 hex digits, or `default`. Never a rule name; administrators map it to a rule in the routing summary. Sent on successful responses (status below 400) that reached routing, cached responses included.

X-Quilr-Served-Model.description: Upstream model id the gateway actually called (on a cache hit, the model of the cached response). Same condition as `X-Quilr-Route`; omitted when the deployment hides model identity, and on streams the gateway had to commit early.

X-Quilr-Token-Count-Source.description: `estimate` when the gateway counted tokens itself instead of the provider (the provider has no counting endpoint, or the model is served through another API).

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Limit of the exhausted quota or app limit (429).

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Remaining allowance of the exhausted quota or app limit (429).

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Unix time (seconds) the exhausted quota or limit resets (429).

X-Should-Retry.description: `false` when retrying cannot help (a budget is exhausted, a zero allowance, or the administrator chose so). OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs honour it.

x-amzn-ErrorType.description: Bedrock APIs: AWS exception name of the error, e.g. `ThrottlingException`.

x-amzn-RequestId.description: Bedrock APIs: request id (the gateway's on gateway errors, AWS's on success).

info.description:
OpenAI Responses API: create a model response (optionally streamed), then retrieve, cancel, delete it or list its input items. Point the OpenAI SDK at `<gateway>/openai_responses/v1`. The current Azure OpenAI SDK (`azure_endpoint=<gateway>/openai_responses` or `<gateway>/openai_responses/v1`) builds the `/openai/responses` aliases. A create runs the app's guardrails, routing, failover and limits; retrieve, cancel, delete and input item listing go to the upstream that stores the response, with the client's query string forwarded unchanged.

Client-facing model APIs of the Quilr LLM Gateway. Each API family speaks a provider's own wire format (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock Runtime, Google Gemini and Vertex AI, and others), so an existing SDK works by pointing its base URL at the gateway. Requests pass through the gateway features that apply to their route (see below), then reach the configured upstream provider.

**Authentication.** Send a Quilr API key (`sk-quilr-...`) or a Quilr-verified JWT. Every family accepts `Authorization: Bearer`, plus the header its provider's SDK uses (listed per operation) and the key headers common API gateways use (`apikey`, `ocp-apim-subscription-key`, `x-apikey`). When `Authorization` is present it decides; send one credential header only. The credential header is never forwarded upstream.

**Bodies.** Request and response schemas document the main fields only and allow additional fields: the gateway forwards provider options it does not know. Do not enable strict body validation that rejects unknown fields.

**Streaming.** Operations that stream return `text/event-stream` (Bedrock streaming operations return `application/vnd.amazon.eventstream`). Disable response buffering for these paths.

**Aliases.** Several paths are aliases of a canonical path (marked with `x-quilr-alias-of`), kept so every SDK base-URL convention resolves. Route all of them.

**Gateway features per route.** Not every route runs every gateway feature. Each model-call operation lists what applies to it in `x-quilr-gateway-features` and in its description: guardrails, Guardian, attachment scanning, model access, routing, failover, limits and quotas, token saving, Prompt Store, response cache. Guardrails do not scan the moderations, images, OCR, completions, files, batches and videos routes (and the Mistral and xAI image, video, batch and fill-in-the-middle routes).

**Gateway response headers.** Most model-call routes relay the provider's own response headers (the endpoint-family routes above do not). The gateway adds: `X-Quilr-Request-ID` (correlation), `X-Quilr-Route` (opaque id of the routing rule that chose the upstream), `X-Quilr-Served-Model` (model actually called), `X-Quilr-Attempts` and `X-Quilr-Failover` (retries and failover), `X-Quilr-Cache` and `Age` (response cache), and the quota headers `RateLimit-Policy`, `RateLimit`, `X-Quilr-Quota-Remaining`, `X-Quilr-Quota-Reset`, `X-Quilr-Quota-Warning`, `X-Quilr-Budget-Overflow` and `X-Quilr-Quota-Scope`. Errors add `X-Quilr-Error-Source`, `X-Quilr-Error-Code`, `Retry-After`, `Link` (help) and, on 429, `X-RateLimit-*`, `X-Quilr-Quota-Id`, `X-Quilr-Quota-Blocked-By` and `X-Should-Retry`. Each header's exact format and condition is under `components.headers`. A provider can never set an `x-quilr-*` header: they are removed from upstream responses. Browsers cannot read these headers from cross-origin JavaScript (they are not CORS-exposed); server-side clients can.

**Guardrail blocks.** A request or response stopped by a guardrail returns 400 with error type `content_policy_violation` and a code: `sensitive_data_blocked` (details give only a count, never the values), `adversarial_content_blocked`, `custom_intent_blocked`, `language_blocked`, `guardian_task_adherence_blocked` or `hallucination_blocked`. Policy and access denials return 403 (`policy_error`). Administrators may replace the message and attach a help link (`help_url`, `Link`). Anthropic-format errors keep the code but not `details`; Bedrock and Google-format guardrail blocks carry no code. Response checks run on non-streaming responses only.

**Redaction.** When a guardrail redacts instead of blocking, detected values are masked in place: fully with `X` characters of the same length (text to speech uses `REDACTED`), or partially, keeping the first and last characters. Request-side redaction changes what the model receives; response-side redaction (non-streaming) changes what the client receives. No field marks a redaction.

**Advisories.** When coding-helper checks are on, a non-streaming response may end with an appended paragraph starting `Guardian note:` about dependency vulnerabilities or newer versions.

**Streams.** While a stream is idle for 15 seconds the gateway writes SSE comment lines (`: ` prefix); SSE parsers ignore them. If the gateway has not answered 15 seconds after admitting a request it starts a `200` event stream early; a later failure then arrives as an in-stream error event carrying an added `status_code` field instead of an HTTP status. Bedrock streams end with an exception frame (`modelStreamErrorException` or `internalServerException`) when the upstream stream is interrupted.

**Error codes.** `x-quilr-error-codes` lists every gateway code (`source: gateway`) and the gateway's names for provider failures (`source: provider`) with their usual status. Codes are only ever added, never renamed. A code marked `also_sent_by_providers` does not by itself say who raised the error: read `X-Quilr-Error-Source` or `error.source`. Responses API ids starting `resp_qtx_` were issued by the gateway for a translated provider and are valid only against the gateway.

post.description:
Creates a model response. `model` selects the model among those configured for the app (the app's routing may choose the upstream). With `stream: true` the answer is a server-sent event stream of Responses events, ending with `response.completed` (or `response.failed` / `response.incomplete`). Guardrails can redact the input or output, or block it (400 with a guardrail code; policy and access denials are 403). Requests that depend on state held by one upstream (`previous_response_id`, `conversation`, stored prompts) stay on that upstream; when that is not possible the request fails with 400 or 409. Responses served by translation to a provider without a Responses API are not stored and cannot be retrieved later.

**Gateway features on this route:** request guardrails, response guardrails (non-streaming), Guardian checks, hallucination check (non-streaming), attachment scanning, model access rules, routing groups, content routing, failover, limits, quotas and budgets, token saving, Prompt Store, universal system prompt.

tags.description: OpenAI Responses API: create a model response (optionally streamed), then retrieve, cancel, delete it or list its input items. Point the OpenAI SDK at `<gateway>/openai_responses/v1`. The current Azure OpenAI SDK (`azure_endpoint=<gateway>/openai_responses` or `<gateway>/openai_responses/v1`) builds the `/openai/responses` aliases. A create runs the app's guardrails, routing, failover and limits; retrieve, cancel, delete and input item listing go to the upstream that stores the response, with the client's query string forwarded unchanged.
tags.name: OpenAI Responses
